originalTitle: Reliance Industries, Jio Financial announce Q1 earnings dates. Check details
simplifiedContent: Reliance Industries and Jio Financial Services are going to share their financial results for the months of April, May, and June soon. This is important because it will give investors an idea of how these companies are doing. Reliance Industries will share its results on July 17, 2026, and Jio Financial Services will share its results on July 16, 2026. Investors are interested in these results because they want to know how the companies' main businesses and financial services are performing. This is a big deal because many other companies will also be sharing their results around the same time, which is called the "results season".

originalTitle: Retail space rent in Delhi's Khan market rises 9pc annually in Apr-Jun: C&W
simplifiedContent:
Here's a rewritten version of the news item in simple language: 
The rent for retail spaces in Delhi's Khan Market has increased by 9% in the last few months. This is a sign that India's housing market is still doing well, even in the second half of 2026. Many people are looking to buy high-end homes, which is helping to keep the market strong. However, the number of homes being sold is slowing down, and there are more new homes being built than being sold, which might lead to developers offering discounts. This could affect the housing market, but for now, it seems to be stable.

originalTitle: India's 10-year bond logs best day in over a week on oil relief
simplifiedContent: Here's what happened in the stock market: Indian government bonds had a good day on Friday because many people wanted to buy them, which means their prices went up and their yields (or returns) went down. This happened partly because oil prices are falling, which made investors feel more positive about the market. Some foreign investors also put their money into these bonds, which helped. Investors are still being cautious because of possible global conflicts and weather issues that could affect the market. An upcoming change involving Bloomberg may also change how the market works, which investors are watching closely.

originalTitle: Kusumgar IPO: Issue booked 136 times on Day 03; NII, QIB portions see huge demand, GMP signals 39% premium
simplifiedContent: Kusumgar Limited's initial public offering (IPO) was very popular, with 136 times more people wanting to buy shares than were available. This means that many investors, including big institutions, wanted to buy the company's shares. The company is selling 1.55 crore shares, but it won't keep the money raised from the sale - instead, it wants to increase its visibility. The shares are expected to start trading on July 15, and before that, they're already being sold in unofficial markets for a premium of ₹163, which is 39% higher than the original price. This suggests that investors are very optimistic about the company's future.

originalTitle: US stock market today: S&P 500, Nasdaq futures slip after tech-led rally; SK Hynix debut in focus
simplifiedContent: The US stock market was expected to open slightly lower on July 10, after having gone up the day before. Despite this small drop, the market is still on track to have a good week, partly because tensions in the Middle East are easing and oil prices are falling. Investors are also looking forward to seeing how a company called SK Hynix will do when it starts selling shares in the US. This is important because tech companies, including those that make computer chips like SK Hynix, have been doing well lately and are expected to continue doing so. The market is also preparing for companies to release their earnings reports, which will give investors a better idea of how well they're doing.

originalTitle: Expert view: Recent correction has provided ample opportunities in large caps, says DSP MF's market strategist
simplifiedContent: A market expert named Sahil Kapoor from DSP Mutual Fund thinks that the recent downturn in the stock market has created good opportunities to invest in large companies. He believes that now is a good time to put money into these big companies, also known as large-cap equities. Kapoor specifically mentions that the private bank and healthcare sectors are looking promising. This matters because it could be a good time for individual investors to consider investing in these areas. Kapoor's insights suggest that investors may be able to find value in these sectors amidst the current market conditions.
